speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing; to begin our assessment, how long do these episodes typically last, and were you able to maintain awareness of your surroundings during them?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status (Infantile Myoclonic Seizures)

The patient's history of recurrent staring, unresponsiveness, hand automatisms (grimacing/gestures), a post-ictal confused state, and a specific "muddy taste" (gustatory aura) is highly suggestive of focal seizures with secondary generalization, rather than typical absence seizures. Given the age of 7 and the specific aura, I need to confirm the semiology and rule out other etiologies.

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI
